{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from Cobalt

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script> -- <nodes> <ranks_per_node> <threads_per_core> [app args...]

# Omitted Cobalt option: -A CSC249ADCD08
# Flux accounting/project selection is site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may be charged to a default account or rejected by policy.

# Omitted Cobalt option: --attrs enable_ssh=1
# Flux has no universal, portable equivalent for Cobalt job attributes.
# Performance implication: SSH into allocated nodes may not be enabled, which can hinder debugging/interactive inspection.

# Dynamic resource calculation based on script arguments
nodes=$1
ranks_per_node=$2
threads_per_core=$3

if [ -z "$nodes" ] || [ -z "$ranks_per_node" ] || [ -z "$threads_per_core" ]; then
  echo "Usage: $0 <nodes> <ranks_per_node> <threads_per_core> [app args...]" >&2
  exit 2
fi

total_ranks=$((nodes * ranks_per_node))
threads_per_rank=$(((64 * threads_per_core) / ranks_per_node))

# Request resources (must come after argument parsing for dynamic values)
#flux: -N ${nodes}
#flux: -n ${total_ranks}
#flux: -c ${threads_per_rank}

# Load up the Python environment
module load miniconda-3/latest
source activate /lus/theta-fs0/projects/CSC249ADCD08/design/graph_sage/env
export PYTHONPATH=""  ## Get rid of the default path from the modules

# Environment
export KMP_BLOCKTIME=0
export KMP_AFFINITY="granularity=fine,compact,1,0"
export MPICH_GNI_FORK_MODE=FULLCOPY
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=$threads_per_rank

# Cobalt used aprun (-n total_ranks, -N ranks_per_node, -d threads, -j threads_per_core, --cc depth)
# In Flux, use flux-run to launch ranks across the allocation.
# Omitted aprun option: -N (ranks per node), -j (threads per core), and --cc depth (core binding policy)
# Flux rank placement/binding is configuration-dependent.
# Performance implication: without explicit per-node placement and binding, MPI ranks/threads may be mapped suboptimally, reducing performance.

flux run -n ${total_ranks} -c ${threads_per_rank} \
  --env=KMP_BLOCKTIME \
  --env=KMP_AFFINITY \
  --env=MPICH_GNI_FORK_MODE \
  --env=OMP_NUM_THREADS \
  python profile_train.py ${@:4}
"
}

Because the resource directives are effectively non-functional, the subsequent `flux run -n ${total_ranks} -c ${threads_per_rank}` may request resources that were never allocated, leading to oversubscription or launch failure.
issues: Hard-coded `64` in `threads_per_rank=$(((64 * threads_per_core) / ranks_per_node))` assumes 64 cores per node; if the platform differs, the computed `-c` will be wrong even if resources were specified correctly.

#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from Cobalt

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script> -- <nodes> <ranks_per_node> <threads_per_core> [app args...]

# Omitted Cobalt option: -A CSC249ADCD08
# Flux accounting/project selection is site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may be charged to a default account or rejected by policy.

# Omitted Cobalt option: --attrs enable_ssh=1
# Flux has no universal, portable equivalent for Cobalt job attributes.
# Performance implication: SSH into allocated nodes may not be enabled, which can hinder debugging/interactive inspection.

# Dynamic resource calculation based on script arguments
nodes=$1
ranks_per_node=$2
threads_per_core=$3

if [ -z "$nodes" ] || [ -z "$ranks_per_node" ] || [ -z "$threads_per_core" ]; then
  echo "Usage: $0 <nodes> <ranks_per_node> <threads_per_core> [app args...]" >&2
  exit 2
fi

total_ranks=$((nodes * ranks_per_node))
threads_per_rank=$(((64 * threads_per_core) / ranks_per_node))

# Request resources (must come after argument parsing for dynamic values)
#flux: -N ${nodes}
#flux: -n ${total_ranks}
#flux: -c ${threads_per_rank}

# Load up the Python environment
module load miniconda-3/latest
source activate /lus/theta-fs0/projects/CSC249ADCD08/design/graph_sage/env
export PYTHONPATH=""  ## Get rid of the default path from the modules

# Environment
export KMP_BLOCKTIME=0
export KMP_AFFINITY="granularity=fine,compact,1,0"
export MPICH_GNI_FORK_MODE=FULLCOPY
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=$threads_per_rank

# Cobalt used aprun (-n total_ranks, -N ranks_per_node, -d threads, -j threads_per_core, --cc depth)
# In Flux, use flux-run to launch ranks across the allocation.
# Omitted aprun option: -N (ranks per node), -j (threads per core), and --cc depth (core binding policy)
# Flux rank placement/binding is configuration-dependent.
# Performance implication: without explicit per-node placement and binding, MPI ranks/threads may be mapped suboptimally, reducing performance.

flux run -n ${total_ranks} -c ${threads_per_rank} \
  --env=KMP_BLOCKTIME \
  --env=KMP_AFFINITY \
  --env=MPICH_GNI_FORK_MODE \
  --env=OMP_NUM_THREADS \
  python profile_train.py ${@:4}
